Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers here, and I've attached a short playbook that maps responsibilities and transfer controls. More detail below and Karthik can add ops specifics.

1) CMK custody and rotation
- MedEx controls the Customer Master Key (BYOK) in private deployments; Redwood never has persistent access to CMK material.
- Operator (Redwood) processes that require decryption (for example, on-boarding data migration) must be executed under a documented, timeboxed breakglass procedure. That procedure requires customer explicit approval and is logged to an immutable audit stream.

2) Operator access constraints
- Operator accounts are limited to maintenance windows and are strictly just-in-time (JIT) with MFA and ephemeral keys.
- No operator access to unencrypted customer data in production under normal ops.

3) Subprocessors / third parties
- For private deployments inside customer VPC or on-prem, we do not route telemetry out of the customer environment by default. Any third-party software components (e.g., managed kernel updates, hardware vendor diagnostics) are disclosed in the subprocessor appendix and require customer opt-in.

4) Cross-border transfer 
- By default we honor the customer's region for all storage and logs. Backups and telemetry do not exit the region unless explicitly configured by the customer.

5) Evidence / SOC2
- Attached is a draft playbook and a pointer to our SOC2 snapshot. Karthik, can you attach the one-page matrix the ops team maintains?

Next steps: I propose we (1) share the playbook now, (2) run through a brief 30-min walk-through with your security team this week, and (3) produce the SOC2 evidence pack and the subprocessor checklist for signature before procurement sign-off.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Sara, Hannah — adding the ops/tech detail Hannah asked for. Below is the operational matrix we follow for private/VPC and on-prem installs. Key points first, matrix attached.

- CMK operations: MedEx holds the CMK in your KMS. Redwood can be granted an ephemeral unwrap token via an HSM-backed signing gateway only during approved maintenance windows. All unwrap events require a recorded approval ticket, and the HSM gateway enforces a TTL that prevents long-lived tokens.

- Rotation: Key rotation is customer-controlled. We provide tooling to orchestrate rotation (re-encrypt artifacts) but the API calls to rotate are signed by customer service accounts.

- Breakglass: In emergencies we have a breakglass flow that (a) requires two customer approvers from an allowlist, (b) creates a time-limited operator session, and (c) writes a signed ledger entry to the audit bundle that you can ingest. We recommend a 1-hour TTL and post-incident rotation on any breakglass unwrap.

- Subprocessors: For on-prem we only use hardware vendor maintenance (e.g., vendor technicians) and our remote-support tooling when explicitly allowed. The attached matrix lists vendor names, scopes, and whether access is out-of-band.

- Telemetry and backups: By default: logs(TRACE/ACCESS) remain in your VPC. Optional telemetry export to Redwood-managed analytics must be enabled in writing. Snapshots/backups can be configured to stay in-region only.

I attached the matrix Hannah requested (kms-responsibility-matrix.xlsx). If helpful, I can demo the HSM gateway behavior in our staging environment during the walk-through.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Engineer, Inference Runtime
